doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Moving to Los Angeles and getting into the Las Vegas union
summary: Wife Margina wanted California; Harold Land pointed him to contractor Jimmy Mullidor, and he got his Vegas union card and joined the Flamingo Hilton band.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So let's talk a little bit about your years in Las Vegas. Could you tell me, first of all, when you -- when you left Dizzy and made the decision that you were going to do something else, did you leave and do something else right away or was there a time when you kinda were trying to decide what you wanted to do and this opportunity came up?
Well, first of all, I was married -- I was married to a lady by the name of Margina and she wanted to move to California because that's where I met her.
Right. Now, this is not the lady from France -­

No, we were divorced. And so, we moved -- I says, "Okay." So we moved from -- we had moved from -- from Forest Hill to Newark and we moved from Newark to Westwood, in -- in Los Angeles. Okay? And so while we were there, I would go and I would do maybe a club date or a concert or something -­

Yeah. I was talking with Howell Land [phonetic sp.], and Howell said, "Moody?" I said, "I wish I could just stay home and be with my daughter." You know, like, because Michelle was just -- she was like, a -- a baby, you know. So what I did was I -- I was talking with Howell Land and Howell was working with Tony Bennett in Vegas. He says, "Why don't you talk to Jimmy Mullidor [phonetic sp.]?" You know, he was a contractor in Vegas.

I says, "Okay." So I called Jimmy Mullidor, I said, "Yeah, come on up." He says, you know, "We'll see." So I went up there and I think I had to stay two months or a month or something and -- in order to get my card.
